ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: After folding a circular paper (with center at point O) along diameter $MN$, and then folding it into six equal parts as shown in figure 1 to obtain figure 2, if we cut along the dashed line $AB$ and then unfold $\triangle AOB$ to get a hexagon star as shown in figure 3. If $\angle CDE = 75^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle OBA$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OC, EO\\
Due to the folding property, we have: $\angle$EOC=$ \frac{360^\circ}{12}=30^\circ$, EC=DC, OC bisects $\angle$ECD\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ECO=$ \frac{1}{2}\angle ECD=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ−2\times 75^\circ)=15^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$OEC=$180^\circ$−$\angle$ECO−$\angle$EOC=$135^\circ$\\
Thus, the measure of $\angle OBA$ is $\boxed{135^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are three schematic diagrams in the figure. Figure 1 is a semicircle with O as the center and MN as the diameter; inside, dashed lines starting from O divide the semicircle by folding into several equal sectors. According to the problem statement, after first folding along the diameter, it is equivalent to the whole circle being divided into 12 equal parts. Figure 2 shows the folded sector-shaped piece of paper, the dashed line AB is the cutting line, and points O, A, B are marked. Figure 3 is the six-pointed star shape obtained after unfolding, with C, D, E marked in the upper right, and the sides corresponding to the cuts near the dashed segment. Reasoning: Connect OC and OE in Figure 3. Since after folding and unfolding it corresponds to a 12-part equal division of the whole circle, the central angle between adjacent corresponding radii is ∠EOC = 360°/12 = 30°. By the symmetry of cutting and folding, EC and DC are mirror-corresponding sides, so EC = DC, and OC bisects ∠ECD. It is known that ∠CDE = 75°. In the isosceles triangle ECD, ∠CED = ∠CDE = 75°, so ∠ECD = 180° - 75° - 75° = 30°. Therefore ∠ECO = 1/2 ∠ECD = 15°. In triangle EOC, ∠OEC = 180° - ∠EOC - ∠ECO = 180° - 30° - 15° = 135°. By the corresponding relationship before and after unfolding, ∠OBA in Figure 2 is equal to ∠OEC in Figure 3, so ∠OBA = 135°.
